chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Khalaf ibn Ḥammād, who said:
I said to Abī al-Ḥasan al-Māḍī عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, a man from your followers asked me to ask you about an issue, so do you permit me concerning it? He said to me: “Bring it.”

So I said: May I be made your ransom, a man married a slave-girl or bought a slave-girl, whether she had menstruated or had not menstruated, and at the beginning of when she first menstruated, when he deflowered her, the blood became profuse, and she remained for days and nights. So the midwives were shown her case, and some said: it is from menstruation, and some said: it is from virginity. He said: Then he smiled and said: “If it is from menstruation, then her husband should refrain from her, and she should refrain from salat (prayer). And if it is from virginity, then she should perform wudu (ablution) and pray, and her husband may come to her if he wishes.”

I said: May I be made your ransom, and how is she to know whether it is from menstruation or from virginity? He said: “O Khalaf, this is a secret of Allah, so do not spread it. She inserts a piece of cotton and then removes it. If the cotton comes out ringed with blood, then it is from virginity; and if it comes out soaked through with blood, then it is from menstruation.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer); the act of worship suspended in menstruation
key_terms.الْحَيْضِ: menstruation; the blood state that prevents salat (prayer) and intercourse
key_terms.الْعُذْرَةِ: virginity; here referring to blood resulting from defloration
key_terms.الْقَوَابِلَ: midwives; women consulted to assess the cause of the bleeding
key_terms.فَلْتَتَوَضَّأْ: let her perform wudu (ablution); the ruling when the blood is not menstrual
key_terms.قُطْنَةً: a piece of cotton used to test the nature of the bleeding

ai.seo_question: How can menstrual blood be distinguished from the blood of virginity in Shia hadith, and what are the legal rulings for prayer and intercourse?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for distinguishing menstrual blood from the blood of virginity after first intercourse. Based on that distinction, it clarifies whether salat (prayer) is suspended and whether the husband must refrain from intercourse, while also teaching a practical method for identifying the source of the blood.
